content.text:
Committed as `75f980e4`.

## Report

**What changed and why.** `docs/test-matrix-format.md` still told an author the matrix is one file carrying three parts inline (artifact inventory, node blocks, and a `## Reference` section). That's the shape the split just ended. I rewrote three sections:

- **Document structure**: now says TEST_MATRIX.md is the core, describes the `## Parts map` table (one row per part file under `matrix/`, naming the row count and the node's `ARCHITECTURE.md` responsibility line), states the body's node blocks and the generated Reference both now live outside the core (the Reference in the committed `TEST_MATRIX.index.md`), and explains the two ways a reader joins them back into one document: `guardrails/specformat.py`'s `spec_paths()`/`read_document()` for gates and builders (core + parts only), and `tests/conftest.py`'s `read()` for the test suite (core + parts + the committed Reference).
- **Node blocks stand as the case grouping**: added that each block is its own file under `matrix/`, named after the node with the `[target]` marker dropped from the filename only, and that a new row is written into that node's own part file, never into TEST_MATRIX.md.
- **The generated Reference**: replaced the "matrix carries a `## Reference` section" framing with the actual committed home (`TEST_MATRIX.index.md`), the real builder (`scripts/build-matrix-reference.py`) and gate (`guardrails/check-matrix-reference.py`) names, and their real command-line shape (core, then parts, then index path).

I dropped the trailing sentence "The gate stays unarmed until the delivery that converts the matrix to this format, and it arms in that same delivery" — that conversion (row 477, `JOURNAL.md` 2026-07-23) already landed a month before this branch's date and the gate is demonstrably armed in `guardrails/pre-push` today, so the sentence was stale for a reason unrelated to this split. I left the "conversion delivery" section (row-477 six-to-five-cell conversion) untouched: it mirrors an identical still-present pattern in `docs/architecture-format.md` for that document's own already-landed conversion, so retaining it appears to be this project's convention rather than a defect.

**Note on the sibling doc**: `docs/spec-format.md` — the file I was pointed to as already describing a core-plus-parts shape — does not actually mention parts, an index, or a shared reader anywhere (verified by full read + grep). I instead modeled the shape on the real mechanics: `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`'s own `## Parts map`, `guardrails/specformat.py`'s docstring and `parts_map()`/`spec_paths()`, and `tests/conftest.py`. Not fixed since it's out of scope (only `docs/test-matrix-format.md` was mine to edit).

**Verification.**
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_matrix_reference.py tests/test_traceability.py -q` → 193 passed.
- `bash guardrails/pre-push < /dev/null` → every gate `OK` except gate a (prover record) and gate m (installed hook drift), both named in the task as expected reds. Gate d (matrix Reference) and gate aa (doc findings bound) are both green.
- The rewrite tripped `scripts/rule-census.py`'s sentence-length cap (25 words) and one "contrast-by-denial" scissors hit; I split the long sentences and removed the "not its whole body" cut. Final count for this page: 30 findings, down from the pre-edit 33, so I re-seeded `guardrails/rule-census.json`'s entry via `python3 scripts/rule-census.py --json guardrails/rule-census.json` (only this page's numbers moved, and only downward).

**Commit**: `75f980e4` on `cut/2026-08-19-matrix-parts`, touching `docs/test-matrix-format.md` and `guardrails/rule-census.json`.

**Full text of every rewritten paragraph** is in the file listing above (lines 23, 26, 28, 30, 48, 54, 56) — reproduced here for the cold readers:

> TEST_MATRIX.md is the matrix's core. The body's other parts live outside it, described below. The core opens with a short preamble, the same shape the family gives it. The preamble states what the document covers, what the bracket codes are, and how the keywords read. Two things follow the preamble, in this order:

> 2. **The Parts map** — a table naming every part file the matrix's rows live in, one row per part. Its order is the order a reader should read the parts in. A part is a file under `matrix/`, holding one architecture node's whole block of rows. The map names each part's row count and its topic line, the node's own responsibility line carried over from `ARCHITECTURE.md`. Together they let a reader judge a part's size and purpose before opening it.

> The matrix rows — the body, grouped into node blocks — live outside the core, one file per architecture node under `matrix/`, never inside TEST_MATRIX.md. The generated Reference, mapping each spec anchor to the matrix rows that cover it, lives outside the core too, in its own committed file, `TEST_MATRIX.index.md`.

> A reader who wants the whole matrix as one document reads it through the shared reader rather than opening TEST_MATRIX.md alone. `guardrails/specformat.py`'s `spec_paths()` and `read_document()` join the core and the parts the Parts map names into one body, in map order. This is the same join the spec's own core and parts already use. A gate or a builder script takes the core, then each part, on its command line, and reads them this way. The test suite goes one step further. `tests/conftest.py`'s `read()` takes that joined body and appends the committed `TEST_MATRIX.index.md` under a synthesized `## Reference` heading. A test that calls `read("TEST_MATRIX.md")` then sees the core, every part, and the Reference, exactly as if the file had never been split.

> Each node block is its own file under `matrix/`, named after the node. Any `[target]` marker is dropped from the filename only, never from the heading text. [... unchanged sentence ...] A new row is written into its node's own part file under `matrix/`, the file the Parts map names for that node, never into TEST_MATRIX.md.

> The Reference maps each spec anchor to the matrix rows covering it. Its committed home is `TEST_MATRIX.index.md`, a file of its own beside the core, the same home `PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md` gives the spec's own Reference. `scripts/build-matrix-reference.py` builds it from the body rows at freeze. It reads each row's trailing anchors and its row id across the core and every part the Parts map names. The file is output only; no one edits it by hand. The builder is a sibling of `scripts/build-index.py`. The table is the matrix's own generated map, the way the spec's committed index is the spec's code-to-location table. [... unchanged ...]

> A gate holds the Reference against drift, `guardrails/check-matrix-reference.py`, a sibling of `guardrails/check-index-generated.py`. It takes the core, then each part, then the committed index path, on its command line, and it reds on three faults: [... unchanged list ...]
